title: sse: fix partial-JSON delimiter ordering and token/event framing for streaming stability
author: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Several production incidents (see SUP-1023) highlighted edge cases in our SSE streaming path where partial JSON payloads and delimiter tokens could be emitted out-of-order across batching boundaries. This manifested as: 1) partial JSON blocks split across SSE events that were emitted in a different order than token generation, 2) mismatched delimiter tokens for partial JSON arrays/objects leading to parser errors on the client, and 3) rare race between KV cache flush and event framing causing duplicated delimiters. Motivation: improve streaming stability for OpenAI-compatible streaming, function/tool calling flows, and structured output consumers. This PR: - Unifies token->event ordering guarantees in the serving runtime so that token emission order is preserved at the SSE event boundary regardless of batching or prefetching. - Adds explicit partial-JSON delimiter state machine to avoid emitting close-delimiters before upstream tokens are fully flushed. - Adds a short-lived per-request frame-serialization lock that prevents race on KV cache flush vs. SSE event flush (keeps scope minimal and async-friendly). - Updates the OpenAI compatibility streaming adapter to respect the delimiter/state changes and to re-order event fragments deterministically for clients that reassemble partial JSON. - Adds extensive unit and integration tests covering partial JSON across batch boundaries, function-calling JSON chunks, and a new flakiness regression test exercised in CI. Checklist:
- [x] Runtime: token->event ordering fix implemented
- [x] Adapter: openai_compat streaming update
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + e2e streaming
- [x] Docs: streaming stability notes + migration guidance
- [x] Backport: release/2026.02 branch PR queued (see linked backport) Related: ENG-4321 (streaming stability epi), ENG-4388 (structured output regressions), SUP-1023 (customer incident).
